docs.title: YHZ-Floor
docs.text:
The complete, verifiable evidence bundle for a pre-registered ownership audit of AI-agent attack success.

Prepared for double-blind review (IEEE S&P 2027, Cycle 2): no author identities, no experimental reruns during packaging, every retained record byte-preserving.

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
A reported AI-agent attack-success number is a property of the evaluation contract that produced it — not an intrinsic property of the agent. The associated manuscript measures the share of each owner through hash-frozen, one-owner-at-a-time interventions on matched cryptographic tasks: 33 registered cohorts, 3,562 retained sessions, plus a 60-session published-protocol audit — every design pre-specified, every number frozen before the first call.

Owner Intervention Registered result Admission regrade fixed bytes; cleanup −0.8 → −32.8 → +3.9 pp; trigger executes in 100/101 traces Information contract 2×2 prompt slots paired one-way in all 16 family members (96/0, Holm 4.04e-28); RC4 + ECDSA nulls; AES-GCM-SIV accepts nothing Session wrapper interactive vs one-shot powered 32-pair null: 0/32 each direction, advantage ≤10.7% (Wilson 95%) Compute allowance declared vs raised 20/50 at 12,000 tokens → 28/50 raised (8/10 task-level); 17 slots transport-unmeasured Execution evidence attribution ablations joins-only 16/44, signatures-only 28/44, combination 0/44

The headline finding of the external audit: a published protocol's declared 12,000-token allowance censors 30 of 60 sessions into unshown reasoning — six of ten task-level pairs are unmeasured, not failed. Raising the allowance recovers the ceiling-censored slots (28/50; 8/10 pairs) under all five evaluator rules. A published rate is only as strong as the allowance it was measured under.

docs.title: 📗 The YHZ-Floor Guide
docs.text:
Everything a reviewer needs: how the audit works, how to run it, how to verify it, and where every number in the paper comes from.

New here? Start with What this is, then this Guide top-to-bottom Want to check a number? Verifying results + experiments/INDEX.md Want to run an experiment? Running experiments Want to plug in your own API? Setup & API Lost in the tree? Repository map

docs.title: 1. The audit model in one picture
docs.text:
Every reported attack-success number is produced by a contract with identifiable owners. The audit freezes everything, moves one owner at a time, and registers the contrast:

flowchart LR
    A["Frozen task(observations, oracle,seeds, budget)"] --> B{"Owner slot"}
    B -->|admission rule| C["regrade fixed bytes-0.8 → -32.8 → +3.9 pp"]
    B -->|zero-reference premise| D["2x2 prompt slotspaired 96/0 one-way"]
    B -->|wrapper| E["interactive vs one-shot0/32 null, ≤10.7%"]
    B -->|allowance| F["12,000 → 32k/64k tokens20/50 → 28/50"]
    B -->|evidence binding| G["attribution ablations0/44 combined"]
    C & D & E & F & G --> H[("Ownership ledgernever pooled")]

The estimand: each share is a paired contrast on shared seeds — an exact-binomial discordance with its interval, reported per cohort, never pooled. The registered family (16 cohorts) carries a Holm step-down at FWER 0.05 with per-cohort Clopper–Pearson bounds.

docs.title: 2. The experiment lifecycle
docs.text:
Every cohort in experiments/ followed the same registered lifecycle — before any model call:

sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Pre-registration
    participant F as Freeze
    participant R as Runner
    participant G as Gateway
    participant A as Analyzer
    participant V as Evidence gate

    P->>P: protocol + grid + falsifiers written down
    P->>F: FREEZE.json (SHA-256 of inputs, seeds, prompts)
    F->>R: runner refuses to start on hash mismatch
    R->>G: per-call attestation (model echo, finish, reasoning tokens)
    G-->>R: results.jsonl (append-only, one row per slot)
    R->>A: closed-form enumeration (stdlib only)
    A->>V: verify_evidence_revision.py (194 checks)
    V-->>V: any amendment recorded BEFORE the run it governs

Concretely (the M1 published-protocol audit as the worked example — see experiments/external_published_audit_20261110/):

# 1. the freeze is live: inputs SHA-256 frozen, hash mismatch refuses to run
cat experiments/external_published_audit_20261110/FREEZE.json

# 2. the runner takes the API key from the environment (never from files)
export AGENTROUTER_API_KEY="sk-..."        # your own key — see SETUP_AND_API.md
python3 run_published_audit_sessions.py    # 6 tasks × 2 labels × 5 seeds = 60 slots

# 3. results land append-only; amendments are recorded before they run
wc -l results.jsonl                        # 60 registered rows, never rewritten
cat PREREGISTRATION_PUBLISHED_AUDIT.md     # Amendments 1–16, each pre-recorded

docs.title: 3. Plugging in an API
docs.text:
The runners speak an OpenAI-compatible gateway. Three rules the whole campaign followed:

  1. Keys live in the environment — never in files, never in git. Every script reads os.environ.
  2. Every call is attested — model echo, finish status, reasoning tokens recorded per call.
  3. Every allowance is declared — the paper's headline finding is that an undeclared allowance censors results; don't reproduce that.

Full details, gateway quirks (the Responses-API transport, the claude-cli User-Agent requirement, the 420 s wall cap, content-filter behaviour), and a redacted config: Setup & API.

docs.title: 4. Verifying the paper's numbers
docs.text:
Three independent layers, none requiring trust:

Layer Command Checks Bundle integrity python3 -B offline_checks.py verify (in reviewer_bundle/) every manifest payload's SHA-256 Recorded-outcome census python3 -B offline_checks.py census the frozen verdict rows, no execution Paper-level gate verify_evidence_revision.py (in the source bundle) 194 checks: needles, arithmetic, Holm tables, page budgets

Per-cohort regeneration is closed-form (standard library only): each cohort's results.jsonl rows → the printed statistic, by one script. Verifying results walks a worked example.

docs.title: 5. Where every number lives
docs.text:
experiments/INDEX.md maps all 60+ registered cohorts to their directory, their paper section, and their registered statistic. Highlights:

Cohort family Paper section Directory The 2×2 family + modern-AEAD wave (16-member Holm family) §5 experiments/info_contract_* The 96-instance power cohort + floor sensitivity §5, Fig 4 experiments/info_contract_aesgcm_random_p021ar_20261103/, experiments/info_contract_aesgcm_c2_floor8000_p026_20261103/ The wrapper cohorts (frozen/extension/powered) §6 experiments/h2_* The external boundary (censuses, HTB grid, NYU panel, frontier repanel) §7 experiments/external_admission_*, experiments/external_rule_* The M1 published-protocol audit §7 experiments/external_published_audit_20261110/ The out-of-domain transfer witness §10.2 experiments/external_transfer_nondomain_20261109/ Attribution ablations + mutation testing §9 analysis/acts_next_phase_20261019_v2/

docs.title: 6. What is not here, and why
docs.text:
• The manuscript: during double-blind review the paper travels through the venue's submission system only.
  • Raw per-turn provider responses (the largest bulk): the per-slot results.jsonl rows and per-slot summaries carry every recorded outcome; raw response dumps remain with the authors and can be shared on request.
  • Anything identity-carrying: the bundle passed a direct-identifier scan (0 hits); frozen records retain a bare mount prefix (/mnt/nvme5/...) — a filesystem location, not an identity.

docs.title: The reviewer_bundle (offline projection)

docs.title: What is deliberately absent
docs.text:
• The manuscript (compiled or source) — venue-only during double-blind review.
  • Raw per-turn provider responses, per-session prompt dumps, execution captures, ops event logs — the per-slot rows carry every recorded outcome; raw bulk stays with the authors.
  • Any author-identity material — scanned out (0 hits).

docs.title: The reviewer bundle
docs.text: The reviewer_bundle/ directory in the repository is the curated offline projection (24,023 manifest files). Its own README, reproduced below, describes its contents, verification commands, and exclusion boundaries.

docs.title: Anonymous reviewer candidate (2026-11-11)
docs.text:
Locally prepared for anonymous review; not uploaded or published. This is an explicitly reduced anonymous projection of the private full candidate, not the entire full package.

The H1-R3 component includes 852 retained sessions and the original sandboxed execute_replay.py. Its retained programs, fixture state, prompts and outputs are byte-preserving copies. Executing retained programs checks outputs; it does not regenerate model responses. See the component README for execution requirements and commands. No experimental evaluation was run while preparing this projection.

The experiment_b, crossboundary/build and heb1_remediation trees retain the anonymous ablation evidence and original policy implementations. These constructed cases establish bounded policy behavior, not deployed failure prevalence or independent benchmark replication.

The external-boundary wave evidence (Amendment-1 regrade lab, Amendment-3/4/5 admission records, the C1 confirmatory review, and the M1 published-protocol audit under namespace external_published_audit_20261110) ships as byte-preserving copies of the frozen per-session records: results.jsonl rows, per-session prompts and raw provider responses, the registered preregistrations, amendments, the ERRATUM_accepted_c2 record, and M1_FINAL_RESULTS. These are the records behind Section 7's external-boundary numbers and the allowance-dependence finding; they are retained observations, not a fresh execution.

The fixed-executor operation_records.jsonl contains the historical twelve recorded successes whose executor clock medians match the manuscript: RC4 0.214196 ms, ChaCha20 0.131647 ms, CBC 1981.556789 ms, ECDSA 6.956233 ms. These are recorded observations, not freshly verified operations. A different later file with the same basename has different clocks and is deliberately not pooled with this cohort.

Identifying signed RQ3 property certificates, their observation records, original provider/archive wrappers, declared-author LaTeX sources and identifying in-toto runner sources remain in the separate private full candidate. Their exclusion preserves signed originals without redaction or re-signing. This projection therefore does not independently reproduce all property-check and in-toto claims. Synthetic fixture truth and synthetic test keys included here are evaluation materials.

COPY_LINEAGE.json preserves copied payload hashes. MANIFEST.json describes this projection independently of original nested manifests. Inspect without executing experiments:

python3 -B offline_checks.py verify

docs.title: Running experiments
docs.text: The full lifecycle of one registered cohort, with the M1 published-protocol audit as the worked example.

docs.title: 0. The rules that make a cohort registered
docs.text:
1. Pre-registration first: the protocol (grid, cells, falsifiers, allowance, halt rule) is written and hashed before the first model call.
  2. Freeze the inputs: tasks, seeds, prompts — SHA-256 in FREEZE.json; the runner refuses to start on mismatch.
  3. Amendments before runs: any change (allowance, retry, scheduling) is recorded as a numbered amendment before the run it governs.
  4. Append-only results: results.jsonl gains rows, never edits; re-runs write to new per-slot files.

docs.title: 1. The M1 worked example (60 sessions end-to-end)
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["PREREGISTRATION_PUBLISHED_AUDIT.mdprotocol PHASE2-EXTERNAL-PUBLISHED-AUDIT-v1"] --> B["FREEZE.json25 inputs SHA-256 + seeds"]
    B --> C["run_published_audit_sessions.py6 tasks x 2 labels x 5 seeds = 60 slots"]
    C --> D{"per slot"}
    D -->|"solved"| E["SUCCESS row"]
    D -->|"reasoning ate the allowance"| F["COMPLETION_TRUNCATED row(30 slots — the censoring finding)"]
    D -->|"content filter"| G["PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE row(10 babycrypto slots — excluded)"]
    D -->|"HTTP 504, zero turns"| H["transport-unmeasured(17 slots — never model failure)"]
    E & F & G & H --> I["results.jsonlappend-only, never rewritten"]
    I --> J["sweep_published_audit.pySWEEP_PUBLISHED_AUDIT.json"]
    J --> K["20/50 at 12k → 28/50 raised8/10 task-level, 5 rules agree"]

cd experiments/external_published_audit_20261110/
export AGENTROUTER_API_KEY="sk-..."
python3 run_published_audit_sessions.py          # registered wave (12k allowance)
python3 sweep_published_audit.py                 # the final scored state

docs.title: 2. What one recorded slot looks like
docs.text:
Every row of results.jsonl is self-describing — here is the shape (fields abbreviated):

{"seed": 501, "task": "eps", "label": "gpt-5.6-sol", "cell": "C1",
 "status": "SUCCESS", "submissions": 1, "turns": 1,
 "oracle_match": true, "byte_exact": true,
 "attestation": [{"model_echo": "gpt-5.6-sol", "finish": "completed",
                  "usage": {"input_tokens": 1544, "output_tokens": 8120,
                            "reasoning_tokens": 7340}}],
 "program_sha256": "…", "stdout_sha256": "…"}

The censoring finding is visible in the rows themselves: the 30 truncated sessions carry submissions = 0 and every turn ending incomplete / max_output_tokens with reasoning_tokens = 12,000 and an empty visible block.

docs.title: 3. Running a different cohort
docs.text:
Every cohort directory follows the same layout — pick one, read its registration, run its runner:

Cohort What it runs Entry info_contract_aesgcm_random_p021ar_20261103/ the 96-instance power cohort (CSPRNG sampling) run_*.py after FREEZE check h2_pairs_powered_20261107/ the powered 32-pair wrapper cohort same pattern external_admission_amend3_20261105/ the NYU three-label panel (168 sessions) run_amend3_sessions.py external_transfer_nondomain_20261109/ the out-of-domain premise witness (16 sessions) the transfer runner

All runners share: environment-only keys, hash-gated freezes, append-only results, per-call attestation, pre-registered halt rules.

docs.title: 4. After the run
docs.text:
1. The analyzer re-derives every printed statistic from the raw rows (closed-form, stdlib).
  2. Amendments that touched the protocol are cross-checked against PREREGISTRATION*.md.
  3. The evidence gate (verify_evidence_revision.py, 194 checks) pins the headline numbers to the source text.
  4. Nothing is pooled: the cohort's paired contrast is reported with its own population and interval.

docs.title: Setup & API configuration
docs.text: Everything needed to point the runners at a model gateway and run a cohort.

docs.title: 1. Environment
docs.text:
• Linux, Python 3.10+ (the analyzers and gate are standard-library only; the runners need requests at most)
  • No GPU, no database — records are flat files (results.jsonl per cohort)
python3 --version          # 3.10+
cd experiments/external_published_audit_20261110/
python3 -c "import json, hashlib, urllib.request; print('stdlib OK')"

docs.title: 2. API keys: environment only
docs.text:
Never in files, never in git. Every runner reads its key from os.environ:

export AGENTROUTER_API_KEY="sk-your-key-here"
python3 run_published_audit_sessions.py

The key is passed to the gateway as Authorization: Bearer … and is recorded nowhere — the per-call attestation stores the model echo, finish status, and token counts, never credentials. A sweep of the entire campaign tree for key-shaped strings returns zero hits (the sk- matches are base64 coincidences inside provider encrypted_content blobs).

docs.title: 3. Gateway behaviour you must know (measured, not assumed)
docs.text: Behaviour Detail Consequence Responses API only these model labels reject /v1/chat/completions outright ("please use /v1/responses") the transport speaks POST {base}/v1/responses User-Agent required the gateway serves the Responses route behind a claude-cli/2.0.0 (external, cli) UA the adapters set it; plain OpenAI-SDK calls without it fail Reasoning budget vs output budget max_output_tokens covers hidden reasoning too — a session can spend the whole allowance in reasoning with zero visible output the allowance must be declared and recorded per cohort (the paper's headline finding) Temperature ignored the backend omits the field runners never send it Content filter deterministic per task artifact, label-independent filter-blocked tasks are excluded from the scored set, never scored as failures Slow-drip sockets connections hang mid-stream for 30+ minutes every call runs under a hard 420 s wall cap (daemon thread + join)

docs.title: 4. Per-call attestation (what every recorded call carries)
docs.text:
{"model_echo": "gpt-6.1-sol",
 "finish_status": "completed",
 "usage": {"input_tokens": 1544, "output_tokens": 8120,
           "reasoning_tokens": 7340}}

The fingerprint audit re-checks every stored call echoes the registered label exactly (65/65 in the frontier cohort; 60/60 sessions landed in the M1 audit).

docs.title: 5. Budget and halt discipline
docs.text:
• Every cohort's registration states its query budget and token allowance before the first call.
  • Budget rows append to BUDGET_LEDGER.jsonl (per-call cost estimates from the gateways' advertised rates).
  • Halt rules are pre-registered (e.g. M1's halt threshold) — an infrastructure halt is recorded as transport-unmeasured, never as a model failure.
  • The published invoice total for the whole campaign (~600 USD across gateways) is disclosed in the paper's §11.

docs.title: 6. Adding a new gateway/label
docs.text:
1. Probe the label first (an unregistered 13-in/21-out call is the campaign's calibration pattern — recorded, never counted as a session).
  2. Register the route in the cohort's _REGISTRATION.json (label, base URL, allowance, seeds).
  3. Record any deviation from the frozen protocol as an amendment before the run it governs.
  4. Substitute labels are disclosed per-label and never pooled: the cross-vendor withdrawal row (Appendix E) is the worked example.

docs.title: Verifying results
docs.text: Three independent layers, from zero-execution to full re-derivation.

docs.title: Layer 1 — bundle integrity (no execution)
docs.text:
cd reviewer_bundle
python3 -B offline_checks.py verify

Checks every manifest-listed payload (24,023 files) against its SHA-256. Expected: integrity: PASS, 0 errors. The census subcommand reads archived records only — it never runs attack programs or contacts anything.

docs.title: Layer 2 — per-cohort regeneration (closed-form, stdlib)
docs.text:
Every printed statistic regenerates from the raw per-seed rows. Worked example — the 96/0 paired contrast of the power cohort:

cd experiments/info_contract_aesgcm_random_p021ar_20261103/
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open('results.jsonl') if l.strip()]
# registered rule: earliest row per (seed, cell), paired C1-vs-C4 on shared seeds
seen, dedup = set(), []
for r in rows:
    k = (r['seed'], r['cell'])
    if k not in seen: seen.add(k); dedup.append(r)
c1 = {r['seed'] for r in dedup if r['cell'] == 'C1' and r['status'] == 'SUCCESS'}
c4 = {r['seed'] for r in dedup if r['cell'] == 'C4' and r['status'] == 'SUCCESS'}
discord = len(c1 - c4), len(c4 - c1)
print('paired C1-vs-C4 discordance:', discord)   # expected: (96, 0)
PY

The exact two-sided binomial p for (96, 0) is 2.5e-29; the Holm step-down over the registered 16-member family gives 4.04e-28 — reproduce the whole table from experiments/ rows with the same enumeration.

docs.title: Layer 3 — the paper-level evidence gate
docs.text: verify_evidence_revision.py (shipped with the source bundle) runs 194 checks: every headline number is pinned to the source text as a case-sensitive needle, per-cohort arithmetic is recomputed from the raw rows (P021AR/P022 cells, Fisher/McNemar/Holm), page budgets are measured, and the abstract echoes the body. Cross-references the build logs and the dist manifests.

docs.title: What the rows prove — and what they don't
docs.text:
• Each results.jsonl row is a recorded outcome: the per-slot verdict under the registered rules, with its attestation block.
  • The rows do not independently re-prove the cryptography (that would require executing the retained programs — see reviewer_bundle/review.py h1r3 for the sandboxed path, and prior_validation/BINDING.json for what the prior validation covered).
  • Censored slots (COMPLETION_TRUNCATED, submissions = 0) are unmeasured, not failed — the estimand is the paired contrast on evaluable pairs, printed beside the all-registered-session sensitivity.

docs.title: The chain of custody
docs.text: COPY_LINEAGE.json (in reviewer_bundle/) records source→destination SHA-256 for every copied payload; MANIFEST.json hashes the assembled package; failed attempts remain separate (no trial added or removed); nothing was executed during packaging. Records retain the originating workstation's bare mount prefix — a filesystem location, not an identity.
